description.en: Ping Wang is an undergraduate researcher at the University of Washington working on making generative models more controllable, adaptive, and aligned with human intentions, through post-training, reinforcement learning, and multimodal learning. Advised by Prof. Noah A. Smith (UW) and Prof. Yi-Hsuan Yang (NTU).
description.zh: 王平是華盛頓大學的大學部學生研究員，研究如何透過後訓練、強化學習與多模態學習，讓生成模型更可控、更具適應性，並與人類意圖對齊，由 Noah A. Smith 教授（華盛頓大學）與楊奕軒教授（臺灣大學）指導。

home.en:
I am an undergraduate in the [Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering](https://www.cs.washington.edu/) at the University of Washington, where I am advised by Prof. [Noah A. Smith](https://homes.cs.washington.edu/~nasmith/) in [Noah’s ARK](https://noahs-ark.github.io/). Since May 2026, I have also been a student researcher in the [Music and AI Lab](https://affige.github.io/lab.html) at National Taiwan University, advised by Prof. [Yi-Hsuan Yang](https://affige.github.io/).

My research focuses on making generative models more controllable, adaptive, and aligned with human intentions. I am particularly interested in post-training, reinforcement learning, and multimodal learning: how models can learn from feedback, how to design meaningful reward signals, and how models can adapt through interaction. I am also interested in how these ideas extend to multi-agent systems, where agents must coordinate and respond to one another in dynamic environments.

Much of my recent work explores these questions through music and audio, including [rubric-based optimization for text-to-music generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03589), [human-aligned evaluation of music transcription](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04511), and [audio-to-symbolic music understanding](/projects/sheetsage-pro). Through these projects, I aim to develop methods that improve how generative models learn, understand, and interact with complex information, with applications both within and beyond music.

I'm always happy to chat about research, music, or possible collaborations. The best way to reach me is by email at [pingw220@gmail.com](mailto:pingw220@gmail.com).
home.zh:
我是華盛頓大學 [Paul G. Allen 電腦科學與工程學院](https://www.cs.washington.edu/)的大學部學生，在 [Noah’s ARK](https://noahs-ark.github.io/) 由 [Noah A. Smith](https://homes.cs.washington.edu/~nasmith/) 教授指導。自 2026 年 5 月起，我也在臺灣大學 [Music and AI Lab](https://affige.github.io/lab.html) 擔任學生研究員，由[楊奕軒](https://affige.github.io/)教授指導。

我的研究關注如何讓生成模型更可控、更具適應性，並與人類的意圖對齊。我特別關注後訓練（post-training）、強化學習與多模態學習：模型如何從回饋中學習、如何設計有意義的獎勵訊號，以及模型如何透過互動來適應。我也對這些想法如何延伸到多智能體系統（multi-agent systems）有興趣，也就是多個智能體必須在動態環境中彼此協調、相互回應的情境。

我近期的研究多半透過音樂與音訊來探索這些問題，包括[文字生成音樂的評分標準（rubric）最佳化](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03589)、[與人類判斷一致的自動採譜評估](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04511)，以及[從音訊到符號音樂的理解](/projects/sheetsage-pro)。透過這些研究，我希望發展能改善生成模型如何學習、理解並與複雜資訊互動的方法，應用範圍涵蓋音樂，也不限於音樂。

歡迎找我聊研究、音樂或合作機會。最好的聯絡方式是寄信到 [pingw220@gmail.com](mailto:pingw220@gmail.com)。

about.en:

Smith](https://homes.cs.washington.edu/~nasmith/) at UW and, since May 2026, with Prof. [Yi-Hsuan Yang](https://affige.github.io/) in the [Music and AI Lab](https://affige.github.io/lab.html) at National Taiwan University.

My research focuses on making generative models more controllable, adaptive, and aligned with human intentions. I am particularly interested in post-training, reinforcement learning, and multimodal learning: how models can learn from feedback, how to design meaningful reward signals, and how models can adapt through interaction. I am also interested in how these ideas extend to multi-agent systems, where agents must coordinate and respond to one another in dynamic environments.

Much of my recent work explores these questions through music and audio, including [rubric-based optimization for text-to-music generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03589), [human-aligned evaluation of music transcription](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04511), and [audio-to-symbolic music understanding](/projects/sheetsage-pro). Through these projects, I aim to develop methods that improve how generative models learn, understand, and interact with complex information, with applications both within and beyond music.
